messages:
morgan: Heads up — after last night's KMS alias rotate some customers' SCIM provisioning jobs are 500ing. Saw bulk deprovision + reprovision errors and a few audit entries saying KMS decrypt failed. Anyone seen this yet?

alex: Not on my radar. Which key/alias was rotated? Any quick logs?

morgan: Alias was `alias/redwood-provisioner` rotated ~02:15 UTC during the maintenance window. Posting snippet from the provisioner logs:
```
2026-03-23T02:18:12Z ERROR provisioner.sync tenant=acme svc=provisioner KMSDecryptError: Decrypt failed: InvalidCiphertextException
2026-03-23T02:18:12Z WARN scim.queue tenant=acme attempt=1 error=500
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot: KMS alias rotate completed by infra-runner at 2026-03-23T02:15:03Z (change-id c9a7).

irina: Did the rotation include a rewrap step for existing envelope keys? If not, decrypt will fail because we store KMS-wrapped envelope keys in the DB for the provisioner.

samir: Good call. Two common causes: 1) alias was pointed to a new CMK without running ReEncrypt/rewrap of stored blobs, or 2) OIDC/service-account claim used in the encryption context changed (aud/subject), so KMS denies decrypt.

morgan: I checked the rotation PR — infra intended a seamless rotation but skipped the rewrap job due to a failing preflight. The preflight failure was noisy and not escalated. Audit logs show rewrap never ran.

alex: If rewrap didn't run, we should either: A) rollback alias to old key (fastest) or B) run controlled rewrap using old key material (requires permission and old key still enabled). Which we can do?

irina: Old CMK still exists and is Enabled. We can point the alias back to the old key immediately while we triage. That will restore decrypt for existing blobs. But be careful: some tenants already retried and got partial state changes; need to reconcile later.

jess: Quick checklist before rollback: confirm old-key-id, ensure no other services depend on the new alias, and notify SRE/channel for any transient error alerts. Also capture a set of affected tenants from the audit table so we can run retries after rollback.

samir: Also verify the encryption context used by the provisioner when it wrapped the envelope keys. If the rotate changed the audience or service account id (we had an OIDC issuer update last week), KMS decrypt might reject even with the old key if context mismatches. Check DB blob metadata.

morgan: Running `psql -c "select tenant, wrap_ctx from scim_envelopes where wrap_status='wrapped' limit 5"` now — top results show wrap_ctx contains `service=provisioner;aud=redwood-provisioner`. That matches current behavior. No obvious aud mismatch.

alex: OK — sounds like alias pointer switch killed decrypt path. I'm going to coordinate rollback now.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: alias update request queued (change-id c9a7-rollback).

morgan: Rolled alias back to old key at 02:26 UTC. After that we saw immediate spike of provisioning retries processing successfully. However, ~120 tenants still show stuck deprovisions (SCIM state mismatch). Logs: `scim: orphaned-deprov: missing target user for deprovision`

irina: That fits a partial-replay scenario. When decrypt failed mid-transaction some jobs could have marked the user as pending-deprovision but never completed. We'll need to run the reconciliation job.

jess: I can run the `provisioner-reconcile --since 2026-03-22T23:50Z --limit 500` job and watch for anomalies. Will post any errant diffs.

samir: Two action items: 1) schedule an automated rewrap (safe controlled path) and verify in a test tenant first; 2) add guard in the rotation runbook so preflight failure blocks alias switch and escalates to oncall. Also add a post-rotate reconciliation window to detect partial operations.

alex: From incident perspective, recommended incident notes: timeline of alias rotate -> preflight fail -> alias switch -> decrypt errors -> rollback -> partial reconciliation. Add CVE triage note: provisioner had a dependency pinned to an older KMS SDK (we upgraded in the rotation PR). That SDK bump exposes better error handling but didn't cause the break. Flagging for vuln triage team to review whether any of the SDK changes require code changes.

morgan: Appreciate it. Quick questions for the runbook change: what's the safest order for rotation so we don't need rollback? My notes: 1) create new key 2) run rewrap job to migrate all envelope blobs 3) verify decrypts from new key 4) switch alias 5) monitor. Is that right?

irina: Yes, and add a canary tenant step after step 2 (verify several real customer flows), and a fail-fast abort if any decrypt error occurs. Also add a step to snapshot the audit log of pending SCIM jobs before switching alias.

jess: I'll add the reconciliation and snapshot steps to the runbook and create a PR for the rotation playbook.

morgan: One last thing — audit logs show an attempt to rewrap by a scheduled job earlier but it errored with a 403 KMS AccessDenied for principal `svc-account:provisioner-rotator`. Does that account need extra IAM permissions to call `kms:ReEncrypt`?

samir: Yes, rewrap needs both `kms:Decrypt` on the old key and `kms:Encrypt` on the new key, plus `kms:ReEncryptFrom`/`To` if using condition-managed policies. Check the rotator's IAM role against both CMKs and the alias policy.

alex: I'll open an infra ticket to add those permissions and gate the rotation until the role + policy are validated.

morgan: Thanks — running reconciliation now, will report back with counts. If anyone sees unrelated 500s in scim queue correlate to this window please DM. :thumbsup:
